correctness.rationale: The proof uses an exact ten-class cover modulo \(48\). Each row has certified exact order \(\operatorname{ord}_q(3)\) and a residue \(c\) with \(3^ac+2\equiv0\pmod q\). The CRT gives \(M=1620742097628261335\) and \(C=206033543146003779\) with \(\gcd(C,M)=1\). Hence every prime \(p>M\) in that progression makes \(3^tp+2\) composite for every \(t\ge0\). The modulo-\(41\) row separately proves \(p\ne3^s+2\) for every \(s\). Defant's Lemma 2.2 then yields the Schemmel-nontotient conclusion for every exponent \(\alpha\). The packaged verifier rechecks all finite modular assertions exactly.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the first Mersenne-excluded parameter of an explicit conjecture in the foundational Schemmel-nontotient paper. It proves an infinite all-exponent family rather than a finite sample and provides an explicit arithmetic progression of primes. The covering-system mechanism is structurally distinct from the source's excluded non-Mersenne construction and can inform attacks on other exceptional parameters.
